# Nexley

> A syllabus-aligned study notebook for NSW HSC Year 11-12 students. Notes and
> classwork file against the actual syllabus, marks are recorded with the
> conditions they were sat under (exam marks and open-notes marks are never
> averaged together), and term planning shows which weeks are over-committed
> before they arrive.

Nexley is a free, offline-capable web app (installable as a PWA). It is not a
question bank and does not predict exam topics or provide model answers — it
organises a student's own notes, marks and time against their own syllabus.

## What it does
- Files notes and classwork against the syllabus dot points they cover.
- Records real exam/test marks, grouped by the conditions sat under, and shows
  which dot points marks were actually lost on.
- Spaced review turns a lost mark into a flashcard automatically.
- Term planning shows what is due each of the next eight weeks and flags
  over-commitment as arithmetic, not a guess.
- Works fully offline; sync is opt-in once signed in.

## What it deliberately does not do
- No predicted band or grade, anywhere in the app.
- No shared question bank or model-answer library (a licensing constraint, not
  an oversight).
- No public leaderboard — a comparison ("comp") is joined by code between
  people who chose each other, never browsable or ranked against a cohort.

## Common questions, answered
- **Is it free?** Yes. No ads, and nothing about a student is sold or shared.
- **Who can read a student's notes?** Only that student. Notes are stored on
  their own device and synced to their own account under database rules that
  make the rows unreachable by any other account. There is no public feed and
  no way to browse another student's notebook. The exceptions are deliberate:
  sending one note to one named person, and a comp, where other entrants see a
  username and a score and nothing else.
- **Does it predict an ATAR or a band?** No, by design.
- **Does an AI mark the work?** Only on request, one answer at a time, against
  marking criteria the student pastes in. It is labelled as written by a model,
  it can be wrong, and an AI mark can never be recorded as a real mark. Notes
  are never used to train any AI model.
- **Is it only for the NSW HSC?** It expects NSW-style outcome codes and dot
  points, but nothing is hard-coded to one curriculum — any pasted syllabus works.
- **How does it differ from Notion, OneNote or Google Docs?** Those are blank
  pages, and a blank page cannot tell a student what they have not written.
  Nexley knows the shape of the course, so it can show coverage, surface
  untouched dot points, and tie a lost mark back to a syllabus point.
- **Can data be exported or deleted?** Both, from inside the app. Deletion is
  immediate and needs no email to support.
- **Who makes it?** One Year 11 student in Sydney, shipping most days.
